Russia’s football player Matvey Safonov, who is currently playing for the French professional football club Paris Saint-Germain (PSG), is one of the ten nominees for the best goalkeeper of the year award, according to the Globe Soccer Awards. The other candidates besides Safonov are Diogo Costa (Porto FC), Thibaut Courtois (Real Madrid FC), Gianluigi Donnarumma (Manchester City FC), Joan Garcia (Barcelona FC), Gregor Kobel (Borussia Dortmund FC), Mike Maignan (AC Milan), Emiliano Martínez (Chelsea FC), David Raya (Arsenal FC) and Unai Simon (Athletic FC). Safonov, 27, has played for French powerhouse PSG since 2024. With the French club, the Russian goalkeeper has won the French championship twice, the French Super Cup once, the UEFA Super Cup twice, the Intercontinental Cup once, and the UEFA Champions League twice. Video: Globe Soccer Awards/X

🌏 The economies of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) adopted the Shenzhen Initiative at the conclusion of the Business Summit, with explicit support for the creation of a regional free trade area and reform of the World Trade Organization. 🤝 The document recognizes mutually beneficial cooperation as the cornerstone of joint development and calls for reducing non-tariff barriers to trade in food products. It also coordinates efforts to utilize both traditional and new energy sources and proposes optimizing the interoperability of cross-border payments through QR codes. 🤖 The declaration supports the use of artificial intelligence and the sharing of digital infrastructure by small and medium-sized enterprises. 🏙️ The business summit was held in Shenzhen, China, as a prelude to the APEC leaders’ meeting scheduled to take place in that city on November 18 and 19, 2026.

Location: Khagaria, Bihar Date: October 29 At an AHP-Rashtriya Bajrang Dal district meeting, a speaker fearmongered over the Muslim population, claiming that Muslims account for 42% of voters in Assam. He claimed that Pravin Togadia had started a weekly Hanuman Chalisa recitation to promote Hindu unity and asserted that it would curb “love jihad” and religious conversions to Christianity. He further claimed that if Hindu women did not fall into “love jihad”, Muslims would no longer have “children-producing factories” and their population would decline. He urged Hindus to buy goods from Hindu vendors even if they were thieves or cheats, so that the money would remain within the Hindu community. Another speaker credited and praised Pravin Togadia for preventing Muslim students, who had secured admission on merit, from joining the medical college run by the Vaishno Devi Shrine Board, and for getting its medical college status revoked.
